title: Sales Enablement: Enterprise Prospect Playbook - Positioning, Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Lena Brooks
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook consolidates positioning and messaging, competitive briefs, pitch-deck guidance, pricing guardrails, representative case studies, and a security FAQ for enterprise prospects evaluating Redwood Inference. Use this doc for deal preparation, discovery framing, and creation of prospect-facing collateral.

Intended audience
- AEs and SEs working enterprise opportunities
- Solutions engineers and pre-sales architects
- Growth marketing for enterprise enablement

Quick summary of Redwood value propositions
- Production-first inference runtime: predictable latency and throughput across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Unified developer experience: same API, tooling, and rollout controls in all environments.
- Cost-aware controls: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations that reduce per-token cost without degrading output quality.
- Enterprise readiness: SLAs, VPC/private deployments, KMS integrations, audit logs, and SOC/ISO compliance evidence.

Positioning & Messaging (Top-line talking points)
- Hook (for CIO/CTO): "Move from experimental models to predictable, cost-effective inference at scale."
- Value pillars:
  - Reliability & Uptime: SLA-backed Dedicated and Private options with automated fallbacks and multi-region routing.
  - Performance & Latency: GPU-optimized runtime, sequence-aware kernels, and KV/prefix caching to meet sub-100ms token latency for common enterprise workloads.
  - Unit-cost control: Intelligent batching, cache reuse, and quantization profiles that typically reduce per-token spend 2-4x for request-heavy applications.
  - Security & Compliance: Private control plane, customer-managed VPC/keys, audit logs, and standard compliance evidence kits.
- Proof points (data-driven):
  - Customer X: 60% lower inference cost vs hosted cloud endpoint after moving to Dedicated with batching and cache.
  - Customer Y: Stable p99 latency < 250ms for a 2k concurrent user conversational product on Dedicated.

Messaging by persona
- Engineering/Platform: emphasize APIs, SDKs, model version pinning, rollout controls (canary/A-B), and built-in tracing.
- ML/Applied Research: focus on quantization profiles, eval hooks, model catalog with vetted performance profiles.
- Security/InfoSec: highlight private deployment options, KMS/HSM support, audit logging, and evidence for SOC2/ISO.
- Product/Business: TCO story, predictable committed throughput (Dedicated), and quality guardrails to avoid regressions.

Competitive Briefs (short battlecards)
- General cloud AI platforms (e.g., large cloud providers):
  - Strengths: breadth of managed infra, integration with cloud ecosystem.
  - Redwood differentiation: inference-first runtime with optimized kernels, unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, and explicit cost controls tied to developer tooling.
  - Objections: "We have cloud credits and native integrations."
  - Responses: "For high-throughput or latency-sensitive products, Redwood's runtime and batching reduce unit economics and improve p99 latency - often at lower cost for sustained workloads compared to pay-as-you-go cloud endpoints."

- LLM API providers (model-focused competitors):
  - Strengths: simple APIs and fast time-to-value.
  - Redwood differentiation: enterprise deployment modes (Dedicated/Private), SLAs, and transparent performance profiles; stronger controls for cost/latency tradeoffs.
  - Objections: "Their models are more convenient."
  - Responses: "Redwood provides the same developer ergonomics plus production-grade guarantees and options to host models privately where data residency or compliance matters."

- Inference infrastructure vendors / self-hosted runtimes:
  - Strengths: total control, on-prem flexibility.
  - Redwood differentiation: managed control plane and ops tooling, rollout and observability features, and optional on-prem packaging that reduces integration burden.
  - Objections: "We can build this in-house."
  - Responses: "Building robust serving + autoscaling + observability is costly; Redwood reduces time-to-production and ongoing ops overhead while preserving control via Private deployments and reference architectures."

Pitch deck outline and recommended slides (enterprise motion)
1. Title: Customer logo + brief tagline (e.g., "Predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference at scale")
2. Early context & pain: common infra/ops challenges (latency, cost surprises, model regressions, data residency).
3. Redwood positioning: product modes (hosted, dedicated, private) and unified API.
4. How it works (concise architecture): serving runtime, batching/caching, smart routing, and deployment abstraction.
5. Performance & cost proof points: benchmarks (latency p50/p95/p99), typical cost reductions vs unmanaged endpoints.
6. Enterprise features: SLAs, dedicated capacity, private deployments, KMS, audit logs.
7. Migration/engagement plan: pilot scope, success metrics, timeline, stakeholders.
8. Pricing and commercial options: starter vs committed vs enterprise licensing.
9. Case study / reference: 1-2 pager with metrics.
10. Next steps & ask: POC, technical deep dive, procurement contacts.

Pitch guidance (talk track bullets)
- Start with measurable outcomes the prospect cares about (latency targets, cost per inference, uptime).
- Use an ROI-centered storyline: "We expect N% lower monthly inference spend within 8-12 weeks after deployment."
- Confirm regulatory constraints early (data residency, on-prem requirements) and suggest Private deployment if needed.

Pricing guidance and guardrails (enterprise)
- Hosted (self-serve): usage-based pricing (per token / per-embedding) for trials and early product-market fit. Ideal for rapid prototyping.
- Dedicated: committed monthly capacity (GPU pool) with throughput-based SLAs. Typical commitments start at 3-6 months. Includes options for burst capacity.
- Private (enterprise license): platform fee + optional on-prem deployment, professional services for install and ops handoff, and annual support.
- Add-ons: advanced observability retention, extended compliance packages, premium SLA and 24/7 support.

Pricing playbook (negotiation points)
- Pilot/POC: 4-8 week discounted trial (credits + limited dedicated capacity). Clearly define success criteria (latency, throughput, cost per inference, functional quality on evaluation prompts).
- Commercial: anchor on committed throughput and predictable unit economics. Use benchmarking data to size the Dedicated pool.
- Discounts: volume and multi-year commitments; reduce unit rates as committed throughput increases. Preserve revenue via minimum commitment floors.

Case studies (condensed templates)
- Customer A (SaaS: conversational support)
  - Situation: rapidly growing concurrency and token volume; unpredictable costs on cloud endpoints.
  - Solution: Moved to Redwood Dedicated with auto-batching and prefix cache.
  - Result: 55% reduction in monthly inference cost; p99 tail latency improved from 1.2s to 320ms; rollout to production in 6 weeks.

- Customer B (FinServ: regulated knowledge retrieval)
  - Situation: strict data residency and audit requirements; needed private model serving.
  - Solution: Private deployment into customer VPC + KMS-managed keys; integrated with existing audit pipeline.
  - Result: Compliance review passed; inference throughput scaled to 400 RPS for internal agent workflows; reduced median latency by 40%.

Security FAQ for prospects (top questions + short answers)
- Q: Where does customer data go in Redwood hosted deployments?
  - A: Hosted API processes request data in-region and stores minimal operational logs. For customers with residency requirements we recommend Dedicated (isolated GPU pools) or Private deployment (customer VPC/on-prem).

- Q: Do you support customer-managed keys?
  - A: Yes. Private and Dedicated options support KMS integrations; Private on-prem installs can use HSM-backed keys per customer policy.

- Q: What audit and logging capabilities are available?
  - A: Audit logs for model requests, administrative actions, and rollout events are available and can be exported to customer SIEMs. Retention and export configurations are part of enterprise enablement.

- Q: What compliance evidence do you provide?
  - A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts; we provide redacted evidence under NDA and can support customer audits via our compliance team.

- Q: How is authentication and RBAC managed?
  - A: Role-based access controls integrate with SSO (SAML/OIDC). Fine-grained API keys and per-route permissions are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments.

- Q: Can I run Redwood entirely on-prem?
  - A: Yes. We offer an on-prem package for regulated or air-gapped environments. This includes deployment automation, health checks, and an ops handoff checklist. Professional services are typically engaged for the initial install.

- Q: What data retention and deletion guarantees do you provide?
  - A: Retention is configurable per-customer. For Private deployments, customer controls retention. For Hosted and Dedicated, we offer configurable retention windows and documented deletion procedures; contractual terms can be provided for stricter guarantees.

Deal preparation checklist (pre-demo / pre-pitch)
1. Confirm stakeholder map and success metrics (who signs off on latency/cost/quality).
2. Identify compliance/regulatory constraints and data flow requirements.
3. Obtain sample payloads and representative prompt sets to run a benchmark.
4. Propose pilot scope (duration, success criteria, technical contacts).
5. Prepare benchmark artifacts: expected p50/p95/p99 latency, cost-per-1M tokens projections, recommended Dedicated sizing.

Operational handoff for pilots (SE to Solutions/Engineering)
- Step 1: Share representative prompt set and sample payloads.
- Step 2: Provision trial environment (hosted credit or small Dedicated pool).
- Step 3: Run benchmark with SE and collect token-level cost and latency.
- Step 4: Iterate on batching and caching configs; apply quantization profile if needed.
- Step 5: Deliver pilot report with recommended Dedicated sizing and projected savings.

Appendix: Example benchmark summary (example numbers for commercial discussions)
- Workload: conversational agent, 64-token average response, 20% long-tail context (>= 1024 tokens)
- Hosted baseline: p95 latency 420ms, p99 1.2s, cost per 1M tokens: $1,200
- Redwood Dedicated (optimized): p95 latency 110ms, p99 320ms, cost per 1M tokens: $480 (includes batching+cache)
- Note: Numbers are illustrative; always run a short pilot for contractual sizing.
